hard_case: one test file mocks the callee module with a constant factory while a second, unmocked file pins the real value

truth.toolchain: node 22.22.0; jest 30.5.2, ts-jest 29.4.14, typescript 5.9.3; edit applied by hand and the test command run on the whole package

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: the edit is the spec's behavior change; the unmocked file sees 130 instead of 140, while the mocked file still sees the factory's 5

reasoning: `priceTwoFiles` returns `fee33(amount - 10)` for amounts above 100, with `fee33` the identity. `test/priceTwoFilesUnmocked.test.ts` has no mock and pins `expect(priceTwoFiles(150)).toBe(140)`; `test/priceTwoFilesMocked.test.ts` has `jest.mock("../src/fee33", () => ({ fee33: () => 5 }))` and pins `toBe(5)`. The edit `amount - 20` fails the unmocked file only. RIPR-SPEC-0243 example 33: `exposed`, `static_limit_kind: mocked_module`, no `typescript_mock_only_observer`, because the unmocked file credits on its own. ripr reports `exposed` with exact_value / strong from both files, names `static_limit_kind: mocked_module` and carries no `typescript_mock_only_observer`, matching the spec and the truth.
